llm.summary: This skill is a disclosed crash-recovery tool, but it installs persistent hooks that can automatically read session history and resume agent work without fresh user confirmation.

dimensions.detail: The behavior stays under the installing user's account and shows no root escalation, network exfiltration, or remote payload retrieval, but broad local session scanning across all agents is under-scoped for users who only want recovery for specific sessions.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The installer copies an executable script into the OpenClaw workspace, creates user-level systemd configuration, and enables a wake service; the referenced template files are declared but absent from the inspected package, so a fresh Linux install may fail after partial changes.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The instructions disclose automatic resume behavior, but they do not provide a narrow allowlist, dry-run mode, or per-session confirmation before resuming prior work.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: User-level systemd drop-in and wake-service persistence are central to the design and are disclosed, but they cause future automatic execution and agent-session control without a new trust decision.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The recovery purpose is coherent, but the capability is high-impact: it scans all discovered OpenClaw agents, reads recent session JSONL files, and injects continuation system events into selected sessions.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you explicitly want automatic recovery across OpenClaw agents after restarts or wake events. Inspect the systemd unit/drop-in files before enabling them, consider using manual invocation instead, and verify uninstall removes the user service, drop-in, copied script, and any partial files left by a failed install.
llm.findings:
[TM1] expected: The uninstall commands remove scoped installed files and systemd entries; the scanner's broad interpretation of rm -rf is overstated because the artifact targets ~/.openclaw/workspace/skills/boot-resume, not the whole home directory.
[SQP-2] expected: Automatic resume-event injection is the stated feature and is documented, but the artifacts do not give enough user control or prominent warning for resuming prior sessions automatically.
[RA2] expected: The persistence finding is materially supported: the installer sets up user-level systemd startup/wake hooks so recovery logic can run after later restarts or wakes.
[LP3] unexpected: The skill's metadata lists binaries and files but does not clearly declare the shell and systemd authority it expects, which contributes to under-disclosure for installation.
[SQP-3] expected: The bilingual English/Chinese README content does not create a meaningful security concern by itself.
[T06] expected: The static persistence finding is accepted in context: the behavior is disclosed and purpose-aligned, but still review-worthy because it persists and can schedule future agent events automatically.
